description: We are building Last Window: a web app that uses live NASA POWER (MERRA-2) data to show whether any place on Earth has already shifted its climate, and whether that change is speeding up, explained in plain language with honest limits. Stack: React, TypeScript, MapLibre. Looking for help with video editing, scientific review of our statistics, and graphic design for the demo.
summary: Last Window is a web app that answers one question for any place on Earth: has its climate already shifted, and is the change speeding up? A user clicks the map and picks a NASA variable (temperature, rainfall, soil moisture, humidity, wind or sunlight). The app fetches over 40 years of live NASA POWER data, runs standard trend and change-point statistics in the browser, and explains the result in plain language, with expandable technical details for scientists. It shows what is changing, where, how much, and whether the change is statistically significant, which is what the Earth System Trend Detective challenge asks for. Users can compare two places, explore a live-ranked board of 31 hotspots, and see Echoes of other places with similar shifts. Every number comes from a live NASA request, and the app openly states its limits, including possible step changes in the dataset itself. It matters because people can check their own local climate in seconds, without a paper or a technical background.
details:
WHAT IT DOES: Click anywhere on Earth (or search a place) and Last Window fetches NASA POWER monthly data for that 50-60 km grid cell, builds annual series from complete years only (1981-2025 for most variables), and computes Sen's slope, a Mann-Kendall trend test, a Pettitt change-point test and a bootstrap comparison of early and recent trends ("change in pace"). Results appear first as a plain-words card with confidence, then as technical details, charts and the exact NASA requests used. Users can also compare two places, see a live-ranked board of 31 hotspots, and see Echoes of places with similar shifts.

HOW IT WORKS: Everything runs in the browser against live NASA POWER requests, with no backend and no API key. Results are cached per grid cell during a session. Possible dataset breaks (MERRA-2 production-stream boundaries and the solar data splice at 2000/2001) are flagged instead of overclaimed.

BENEFITS AND GOALS: People can check, in seconds, whether their local climate has shifted and how sure we are. We hope it helps students, farmers and local planners ask better questions and look at NASA data themselves.

TOOLS: React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind, MapLibre GL, Recharts, Vitest; NASA POWER (meteorology from MERRA-2; solar from GEWEX SRB and CERES SYN1deg) and NASA GIBS imagery; OpenFreeMap, Esri and Photon for maps and search; Vercel hosting; MIT-licensed open code.

SUPER INTELLIGENCE (SI): Claude (Anthropic) was used for planning, review and drafting text. The team chose the challenge, set the requirements and reviewed all output. All statistics are standard published methods covered by unit tests, and the team checked results against live NASA responses.
